diagnostic_evidence.quote:
More carefully, $A_j$ should be referred to as the  ``volume flux (per unit depth into
the page)'' out of hole

issues.failure_explanation: For velocity \nabla\phi=(\phi_x,\phi_y), the volume flux across a curve is the normal integral \int(\phi_x\,dy-\phi_y\,dx)=\int d\psi, i.e. the change in the streamfunction/harmonic conjugate. The displayed \phi_x\,dx+\phi_y\,dy=d\phi is the tangential differential of the velocity potential; its closed-loop integral is a potential jump/circulation, not the source-sink flux, and it contradicts the paper's own definition A_j=\int\partial_\nu u=\int\partial_\sigma v.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed integrand by the normal flux \phi_x\,dy-\phi_y\,dx, equivalently \partial_\nu\phi\,|dz| or d\psi, and keep the interpretation as the change in the streamfunction.
issues.overall_effect: The fluid-dynamical motivation and source/sink interpretation are stated with the wrong differential. The later formal flux quantity \int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu u used in the theorems is not itself changed.
issues.title: Fluid flux formula uses tangential integral dphi instead of normal flux dpsi
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local replacement of one motivational displayed formula; no formal result, hypothesis, rate, or algorithm depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's own conversion of \mathcal{D}[\phi] into a real part uses the complex measure d\xi in the (\zeta-\eta_1) term, and the stated period jump of \Im f_\mathcal{D} also contains -\int\phi\,d\xi. With |d\xi| there instead, the claimed identity \Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi]=\mathcal{D}[\phi] is false: for example, for \phi\equiv1 on a circular hole the leading Cauchy term integrated with |d\xi| vanishes at the center, whereas the d\xi Cauchy integral gives the residue value needed for \mathcal{D}[1]=1-|D_j|/b inside the hole.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In eqn: complex double layer, replace the measure |d\xi| in the (\zeta(z-\xi)-\eta_1(z-\xi)) integral by d\xi, keeping the \Re[d\xi] correction term, and use the same d\xi form in the Plemelj jump step; the derivation already present in the proof then gives \Re f_\mathcal{D}=\mathcal{D} and the stated period jumps.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem: Complex layer(1)-(2) do not hold for the displayed f_\mathcal{D}. Consequently the arguments using \Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi]=\mathcal{D}[\phi] to prove the nullspace description in lem: properties double layer(4), the dimension statement used in lem: properties double layer(5), and the injectivity in lem: characteristic(2) are unsupported as written; the M>=2 Dirichlet representation proof in thm: dirichlet inherits this gap.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential integrates the Cauchy-Weierstrass term against |d\xi| instead of d\xi
issues.why_classification: The repair is the single measure correction already forced by the paper's derivation; it restores the same construction and all downstream statements without changing hypotheses, conclusions, rates, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Since z-\overline z=2i\,\Im z, one has (z-\overline z)^2/(8b)=-(\Im z)^2/(2b), not +(\Im z)^2/(2b). Thus the displayed f_G has real part -\frac1{2\pi}\log|\vartheta_1(z)|-(\Im z)^2/(2b), contradicting eqn: green and the assertion G=\Re f_G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the quadratic term to -\frac{(z-\overline z)^2}{8b} (equivalently write the real term +\frac{(\Im z)^2}{2b}) and correct the algebra (2\Im z)^2 to (2i\Im z)^2.
issues.overall_effect: Only the standalone complex representation of G in lem: Complex layer(3) is false; it is not used in the later potential-theoretic arguments.
issues.title: Wrong sign in the quadratic term of f_G
issues.why_classification: This is an isolated local sign correction with no dependent results and no loss of mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we approximate the modified single-layer potential \( \mathcal{S}_0 \)

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete analogue of \mathcal S_0[\phi]=\mathcal S(I-\mathcal M)\phi+\mathcal M\phi is S(I-M)+M, not S(I-M). The stated generalized eigenproblem therefore is not a discretization of e: steklov bie; it also makes both sides annihilate constant density vectors, leaving the constant component of \vec\phi undetermined even though the later reconstruction u(z)=\overline\phi+\sum G(z-z_j^k)(\phi_j^k-\overline\phi)h_j^k adds that constant back into the eigenfunction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Form the right-hand matrix as S(I-M)+M, equivalently solve for \psi=(I-M)\phi with the constraint M\phi=-M S\psi and reconstruct the zero-mean Dirichlet trace (I-M)S\psi.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Nystr"om/eig procedure does not encode the stated modified single-layer representation: the pencil is singular on constant densities and a reconstructed nonzero eigenfunction can be shifted by an arbitrary constant, violating \partial_\nu u=\sigma u unless the correct mean condition is imposed. The continuous theorem thm: steklov is not itself disproved, but the asserted discrete analogue is mismatched.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the averaging term in the modified single-layer potential
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained rank-one averaging term (or an equivalent local projection) in one displayed discrete system; it preserves the continuous theorem, the method, and the advertised spectral convergence.
